title: Which number is right?
concept: Two systems. Two answers. No single source of truth.

captions.ig:
Your sales report says one number. Accounting says another. Same month, same company — two different answers.

So someone loses an afternoon reconciling them by hand. The data isn't wrong; it just lives in two places that never agree.

One source of truth: entered once, every report reads from it. When the numbers come from one place, they can't disagree.
captions.li:
Two systems, two numbers, one very familiar afternoon.

The sales report says $128k. Accounting says $121k. Same month, same company. Nobody's data is "wrong" — it's just kept in two places that were never designed to agree, so someone reconciles them by hand and everyone quietly picks the number they trust.

The fix isn't a better spreadsheet. It's a single source of truth: the figure is entered once, and every report — sales, finance, the board deck — reads from that one place. When the numbers come from one system, they can't disagree.

You shouldn't have to guess which system to believe.

Artifex Labs — business technology that works together.
